title: Mira L. Sedgewick v. Harborline Support Services, LLC
jurisdiction_basis: 28 U.S.C. §§ 1331, 1291; 29 U.S.C. §§ 207(a)(1), 216(b); final judgment disposing of sole federal claim; private represented parties.

timeline.description: Sedgewick begins hourly nonexempt customer support employment.
Supervisor sends team reminder about completion of assigned cases.
Plaintiff asks supervisor about closing time and time entry.
Last of four relevant payroll periods paid.
Payroll corrects separate previously submitted missed-punch request.
Order granting summary judgment and separate judgment entered.

issues.question: Whether the evidence, viewed for the nonmovant, permits a reasonable jury to find uncompensated overtime work and actual or constructive employer knowledge under the FLSA.
issues.standard_of_review: De novo; Rule 56 nonmovant reasonable inferences, substantive FLSA knowledge and worktime requirements.
issues.preservation_status: Raised in opposition and June 29 hearing; resolved in final summary judgment.
issues.appellant_theory: Specific after-punch user events and supervisor communications support inference of work and knowledge; correction process does not automatically defeat liability.
issues.appellee_theory: Event timestamps do not measure continuous work, general reminder and prompt direction to correct time do not establish employer knowledge of actual uncompensated work; no reliable weekly duration evidence.
issues.appellant_relief: Vacate summary judgment and remand for further proceedings.
issues.ruling_quote: Defendant's motion for summary judgment is granted.
issues.preservation_quote: The record permits a reasonable inference of work and employer knowledge.

brief_record_refs.quote: Under Tolan v. Cotton, 572 U.S. 650, 656–57 (2014) [[AUTH:TOL:P1]], the court must credit the nonmovant's evidence and draw justifiable inferences in her favor. Plaintiff's recollection of completing assigned notes may support an inference that some activity occurred after a punch. Yet the timestamps are not measurements of active work. The custodian explains that the server records accepted events and that composition, transmission and acceptance are distinct. IDEP 3–10, 16–20. Plaintiff does not recall a reliable duration and expressly disclaims equating the elapsed intervals with work. PDEP 8–13, 16, 22, 26.
